title: Open-source relay, self-host mode, and zero-cost reference deployment
objective: Complete the open-source relay as a first-class self-hostable service with zero mandatory cost: the authorization server endpoints over the SG-000054 vocabulary with device-backed pairing enrollment, durable local relay state, explicit hard quotas with fail-closed no-billing overflow behavior, a self-host runtime with configuration validation and container packaging, local `cotra remote enable` and `cotra remote pair` enrollment, and a documented free-tier reference deployment that is never required.

include: authorization-server metadata, authorization, token, revocation, and dynamic client registration endpoints implementing the SG-000054 checks, with pairing-code entry on the authorization page and no password, implicit, or client-credentials grant

device-backed pairing enrollment: STRONG-gated local `cotra remote enable` creating the device key and `cotra remote pair` creating a one-time pairing transaction whose hash is registered with the relay over the device channel, with local confirmation of the exact client, scopes, and connection before the device records the pairing
refresh token renewal at the token endpoint that requires a fresh family-bound device-key proof obtained over the live device channel
durable relay state in a local file store with atomic writes, integrity checks, bounded size, and deletion on revocation, holding no payloads, tokens, or device private keys

explicit configurable quotas with hard ceilings for requests, sessions, devices, registrations, pairing attempts, and token issuance, and a no-billing overflow mode that fails closed with typed errors instead of scaling or paying
self-host runtime: validated configuration file, relay entrypoint, container image definition with pinned base, health endpoint, and operator documentation including TLS termination
a free-tier reference deployment definition and documentation that is optional, with self-hosting as the canonical zero-cost path
exclude: any paid API, paid cloud, paid database, paid identity provider, or paid relay requirement
automatic paid overflow or autoscaling into billed capacity
provider-specific client identification or directory submission (SG-000067 onward)
SOCKS, CONNECT, arbitrary TCP, generic HTTP proxying, arbitrary WebSocket forwarding, raw shell tunnels, or any generic executor
any change to the local tool registry, schemas, capabilities, approvals, or the cotrad remote-session lease semantics
claims that a hosted reference deployment is live unless it is actually deployed and verified

authority_delta.filesystem: The relay writes only its own state directory. On the device, enrollment writes only the device key, uplink configuration, and revocation list under the Cotra state directory.
authority_delta.network: The relay listens for the public edge, authorization endpoints, and device channel; it makes no outbound requests.
authority_delta.secrets: Device private keys never leave the device; relay token signing keys stay in relay state; no secret is logged.
authority_delta.approval: Device enrollment and pairing require STRONG local presence; the relay cannot create, widen, renew, or extend a remote-session lease.
authority_delta.privileged: Enrollment and pairing are local PRIVILEGED lifecycle operations never exposed as MCP tools.

invariants: self-hosting works independently of any Cotra-operated relay at zero mandatory cost
quota exhaustion fails closed with typed errors and never overflows into paid capacity
a stolen refresh token cannot renew while the bound device is offline
pairing proves device possession only and grants no workspace trust, approval, or lease
the SG-000052 through SG-000056 vocabulary stays frozen

acceptance.claim: A standards-based OAuth 2.1 client can register, authorize with PKCE through device-backed pairing, exchange and refresh tokens with fresh device proof, revoke, and then reach the paired device through the public edge against a self-hosted relay.
Relay state is durable, integrity-checked, bounded, and payload-free; quotas are explicit with hard ceilings and fail closed with typed errors in no-billing mode.

Self-host mode runs from a validated configuration and container definition with operator documentation, and the optional free-tier reference deployment is documented without being required or claimed live unless verified.
Exact-head CI including release qualification and supply-chain audit, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000058: The P15 adversarial and chaos exit may proceed only after SG-000057 closes with the self-hostable relay qualified.

done_when: The open-source relay is canonical as a self-hostable zero-cost service with device-backed OAuth enrollment, durable state, hard fail-closed quotas, and documented optional free-tier deployment.

canonical_evidence.authority_boundary: Self-hostable open-source relay with authorization server, device-backed pairing, device-proof refresh, durable payload-free state, hard fail-closed quotas, and container packaging, plus STRONG-gated local enrollment. No outbound requests from the relay, no proxy, executor, MCP tool, schema, capability, approval, or lease authority, and no paid dependency or paid overflow.
